  MEMORANDUM

 TO:  City Council Newspaper/Advertising Ad Hoc Committee Liaisons

 FROM:  Huma Ahmed, City Clerk
  Michelle Ramos-Vergara, Deputy City Clerk

 DATE:  February 26, 2024

 SUBJECT:  Discussion of Online Metrics Requirement for Future Audits, and
  Review of the Annual Draft FY 2024-25 Advertising and Notices Bid

 ATTACHMENTS:  1.  Draft FY 2024-25 Advertising and Notices Bid

INTRODUCTION

The City is required to provide an annual bid for legal advertisements with locally adjudicated
newspapers in Beverly Hills. Historically, the bid has also included display advertising as part of
the overall process.

In June 2023, the City Council approved formal bids as submitted by three adjudicated
newspapers: the BH Courier Acquisition, LLC (Courier), Beverly Hills Weekly (Weekly), and
Beverly Press/Park La Brea News (Beverly Press). The publications do not need to submit a new
audit for this year, but will need to do so next year for FY 2025-2026.

The City Council liaisons are provided with this report and if approved, to direct staff to release
the annual bid. This report is an attempt to process the bids in a timely manner.

Staff requests the City Council Liaisons provide guidance on the following:

  1. Online metrics (including social media) which will be required as part of future audits.
  a. The 12-month audit period as the newspapers work on preparing new audits for
  the FY 2025-26 Bid, should be from October 2023 to September 2024.
  2. The draft FY 2024-25 Advertising and Notices Bid.

DISCUSSION

At the June 6, 2023 City Council Study Session, the City Council accepted responses to the
Advertising and Notices Bid 24-070-01 (RFB) from the Courier, Weekly, and Beverly Press.

All three newspapers included with their bid, an independent verified circulation audit which was
conducted by the Circulation Verification Council (CVC). The Weekly and the Press each
submitted audits in the 12-month audit period of October 2021 to September 2022 as required by
the bid. At that time, the Courier submitted a deviation to the audit period requirement
indicating that they wanted the City to gauge their performance based on the most current
available data. Their 12-month audit period was April 1, 2022 to March 31, 2023.
 As has been followed in previous bid solicitations, all proposers wilL be required to furnish an
independent verified circulation audit completed within the last twelve (12) months. Exempt from
this requirement are any bidders who submitted a verified circulation audit to the City of Beverly
Hills in connection with a previous bid if the previously submitted audit was completed within the
twenty-four (24) months prior to the Date of Request of the Request for Bid. Because all three
newspapers submitted an audit with their last bid that was accepted by City Council, a new audit
will not be required until the FY 2025-26 Bid. Again, the dates for the audit period should
be from October 2023 to September 2024. The aforementioned three publications will need to
submit a new audit report next year in early 2025 if there is an interest by them.

The City Council has for many years awarded the bid based on the highest circulation in Beverly
Hills as provided within their audit report. Based on the data provided in the CVC audit from last
year by all three newspapers, the City Council unanimously agreed to award the Bid to the Courier
because it continued to have the highest circulation in Beverly Hills amongst the three
publications. They also agreed to contract with the Weekly and the Beverly Press for display
advertisements and legal advertisements at the Beverly Hills rate of circulation compared to the
Courier’s for additional as needed advertising.

Newspaper/Advertising Ad Hoc Liaisons may also wish to reconfirm and remind each newspaper
to have their next CVC audit include online metrics data when their audits are renewed.

The Circulation Verification Council (CVC) offers some online metrics for its audit reports. ff

FISCAL IMPACT

The City Clerk Office’s FY 2023-24 budget for legal advertising and notices is $112,482. The
Citywide FY 2023-24 budget for display advertising is $537,058. The total advertising budget is
$649,540. After the June 6, 2023 City Council award direction, the funds were earmarked for
advertising in the Courier, the Weekly, and the Beverly Press. There are no set fixed amounts
designated for each newspaper advertisements are placed as needed. It is at the City’s
  -

discretion to place non-legal (display) advertisements in any publication.

Staff respectfully requests the Liaisons review and provide feedback on:

  1. Online metrics (including social media) which will be required as part of future audits.

OVERVIEW AND BACKGROUND

The City of Beverly Hills (“CITY’) requests bids from qualified newspapers (“CONTRACTOR”) to
publish legal notices and display advertisements as required by the CITY.

Beverly Hills is located in the middle of Los Angeles County, surrounded by the cities of Los
Angeles, West Hollywood, Santa Monica, and Culver City. Within its 5.7 square mile area, Beverly
Hills has approximately 35,000 residents, with a business and commercial base that ranks
alongside cities with populations of several hundred thousand.

Internationally recognized for its alluring retail stores, hotels, and exclusive attractions, Beverly Hills
attracts visitors from around the world. As a full-service city, police, fire, water treatment, refuse
collection, and building inspections, among other municipal services, are provided directly by the
CITY.

Throughout the year, CITY prints display advertising to promote CITY sponsored events. The CITY
is also legally required to print public notices (legal advertisements) such as Public Hearing Notices,
ordinances, resolutions, and certain Requests for Bids.

Per California Public Contract Code Section 20169 the City Clerk’s Office conducts an annual Bid
for legal advertising and notices. While not a requirement, the City has historically also included
display advertising in the Bid process.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

In order to qualify to submit a bid in response to this solicitation, CONTRACTOR must operate a
newspaper that has been adjudicated as a newspaper of general circulation as defined in Section
6008 of the Government Code, for the CITY.

OBJECTIVES AND SCOPE OF WORK

The following Scope of Work shall apply to this project:

  1. CONTRACTOR shall enter into an agreement with CITY for services from July 1, 2024
  through June 30, 2025 (see Attachment A for sample agreement).

  3
 Title: NEWSPAPER ADVERTISING SERVICES  Bid No. RFB-25-070-01

  2. CONTRACTOR shall print, and publish on a non-exclusive basis, correctly and in a first-
  class manner in a newspaper that has been adjudicated as a newspaper of general
  circulation as defined in Section 6008 of the Government Code, for the CITY, all legally
  required advertising and any other notices or advertising of whatever kind or nature that may
  be requested in writing by an officer, board, commission or department of the CITY, to be
  printed pursuant to the terms of this bid, and furnish proof of such publication.

  3. Nothing in this Request for Bid (RFB) shall be construed to require CITY to place all
  advertisements, or any particular advertisement, with any CONTRACTOR to whom a
  contract is awarded. CITY retains the right to place advertisements in any publication or
  medium as required by law and as it determines to be in the best interests of the CITY.

  4. Legally required advertisements can be display ads such as Public Hearing Notices and
  Summarized Ordinances which are normally placed in the “front pages”. Legally required
  advertisements can also be classified ads such as full length ordinances, full length
  resolutions, and certain Requests for Bids (RFBs) which are normally placed in the “back
  page(s)” of a newspaper.

  5.  If specified by CITY in writing, up to one full page of legal or display advertisements shall be
  inserted with best effort upfront within pages 1-10 or in the first half of the newspaper if the
  newspaper is greater than 20 pages. Exceptions include last minute advertisements in which
  case, placement can be based on availability of space and with the mutual agreement by
  CITY. Other exceptions include legal/classified ads such as full length ordinances, full length
  resolutions, and certain Requests for Bids and Requests for Proposals.

  6.  Unless CITY specifies a different font style and font size, CONTRACTOR shall publish
  CITY’s legal notices and advertising in the following font style and size:

  serif= Times New Roman eight point font
  san serif Arial seven point font

  CITY will not be responsible for any additional charges for CONTRACTOR’s use of larger
  font sizes, unless requested by CITY in writing.

  7. CONTRACTOR shall accept digital transmission of legal notices and display advertisements
  from CITY. Written copy furnished by CITY shall not be photocopied and published in as is”
  condition unless expressly authorized by CITY. All such written copy shall be typeset as
  required in the font style and size specified above unless otherwise specified by CITY. CITY
  may also provide CONTRACTOR with a camera-ready copy.

  8. CONTACTOR shall provide a proof prior to publication for CITY to review for accuracy.
  Unless CITY specifies a different font style and font size, CONTRACTOR shall submit the
  proof of publication in the font styles and sizes listed above. All CITY advertisements shall
  be approved by CITY in writing prior to publishing. CONTRACTOR shall provide one affidavit
  of publication within two weeks of each publication.

  9. CONTRACTOR shall contact CITY first and within 24 hours of the distribution day of the
  papers to offer any last minute display opportunities at a competitive rate determined by the
  publication.

  10. All advertisements shall be inserted in every edition of the newspaper issued upon the day
  of publication, and not in any supplement thereof, and shall be published for the number of
  days directed in writing by CITY requiring such publication and no more. If the newspaper is
  published on more than one day per week, then advertisements shall be placed on the
  publication date requested by CITY.

  11. CONTRACTOR’s deadline for publication of notices/advertising, space reservation and
  materials submission for publishing shall be as provided in the agreement between
  CONTRACTOR and CITY.

  12. If at any time during the period of the agreement, the newspaper to which the agreement is
  awarded is not published and circulated regularly on its regular date of publication, CITY has
  the right to immediately terminate the agreement and to recover any damages from
  CONTRACTOR.

  13. In the event CONTRACTOR fails to publish an advertisement or notice or publishes
  improperly, CONTRACTOR shall, at the election of CITY, republish on the next available
  publication date at no charge to CITY or shall not charge CITY for the improperly published
  advertisement.

  14. CONTRACTOR will be required during the term of the agreement to deliver free of charge
  fifty (50) copies of each issue of said newspaper to CITY Hall Attn: City Clerk’s office.

  Only one transmittal letter need be prepared to accompany all copies of the bid. The
  transmittal letter should include the name, title, address, phone number, and original

  The bid shall clearly identify the CONTRACTOR’s legal name and address and the legal

  2. Certification of Legal Adjudication.

SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS

Any submission shall constitute an irrevocable offer for one hundred eighty (180) days following the
deadline for its submission. Information contained in the bid is confidential and shall remain so until
a contract is signed. A bidder’s proposal may be withdrawn at any time prior to the bid opening. No
bid may be withdrawn after the bid opening. Violation of this policy may cause bidder’s removal from
qualified Bidder’s List.

  1. Submittal Deadline
  CONTRACTORs shall email one (1) digital copy of bid in PDF format no later than 5:00
  p.m. Pacific Standard Time, on Friday, TBD by emailing the City Clerk at
  cityclerkbeverlyhills. org.

  2. Contact
  CONTRACTORs shall not contact the CITY’s Mayor, Councilmembers, or staff during this
  RFB process regarding the RFB other than the designated RFB Administrator (City Clerk
  Huma Ahmed or her designee). Only CONTRACTORs currently under contract with the
  CITY may have contact with the Mayor, Councilmembers, and staff, however the current
  CONTRACTOR MUST NOT discuss this RFB with the CITY’s Mayor, Councilmembers, or
  staff during this RFB process or they will be disqualified.

  3. Rejection of Bids
  Bids received after 5:00 p.m. Pacific Standard Time, on Friday, TBD shall be considered
  late. Late submittals will be rejected and will not be considered for review.

  The CITY reserves the right in its sole discretion to reject any or all submissions in whole or
  in part for any reason without incurring any cost or liability whatsoever. All bids will be
  reviewed for completeness of the submission requirements. If a bid fails to meet a material
  requirement in the RFB, or if it is incomplete or contains irregularities, the bid may be
  rejected. A deviation is material to the extent that a response is not in substantial accord with
  the requirements in this RFB.

  Immaterial deviations may cause a bid to be rejected. The CITY may or may not waive an
  immaterial deviation or defect in a bid. The CITY’s waiver of an immaterial deviation or defect
  shall in no way modify the RFB or excuse a CONTRACTOR from full compliance with the
  remaining RFB.

  Bids that contain false or misleading statements may be rejected if in the CITY’s opinion the
  information was intended to mislead the CITY regarding a requirement of the RFB. Bids may
  be rejected in any case where it is determined that the bids are not truly competitive, or
  where the costs presented are not reasonable.

  5. Conflict of Interest
  CONTRACTOR shall have no interest in other projects or independent contracts that conflict

  services to be provided pursuant to this RFB. If this CONTRACTOR has no conflict of

EVALUATION CRITERIA AND SELECTION PROCESS

  A. Evaluation
  An Evaluation Criteria has been established by the CITY’s Newspaper/Advertising Ad Hoc
  Committee. The CITY reserves the right to establish criteria and weight factors. Selection of
  qualified proposers will be based on the following criteria as set forth herein. Criteria are
  listed in random sequence and are not considered in any rank or order of importance. The
  bid will be evaluated by the Evaluation Committee on the basis of the response to all
  requirements of this RFB. The following criteria will be used in evaluating bids:

  1. Qualifications, including proof of legal adjudication and results of latest circulation
  audit, to determine effectiveness of each proposer with regard to reaching the CITY’s
  target audience and exposure of advertisements. The circulation audit results will
  weigh heavily during the Evaluation and Criteria process.

  2. Ability to provide services as outlined in the scope of work.

  3. Ability to reach a large readership base, as demonstrated by audited circulation figure
  of publication.

  4.  Demonstrated compliance with the Scope of Work, including ability to publish per legal
  square inch/classified and display advertisements in the size, format and location
  specified by the CITY.

minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Newspaper Ad Hoc Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Monday, February 26, 2024
  4:00 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  February 26, 2024 / 4:31 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Vice Mayor Lester Friedman, Councilmemebr Lili Bosse, Deputy City
  Manager Keith Sterling, City Clerk Huma Ahmed, City Attorney Laurence
  Wiener, Public Information Manager Lauren Santillana

  1) Public Comment:
  a. Lisa Bloch: Publisher of the Beverly Hills Courier
  i. Has asked to be allowed to do the FY 2025-26 audit in the calendar year
  2024.
  ii. Also asked for any other major newspapers that the city advertises with to
  also undergo an audit.
  iii. She also asked why the city requested the online metrics of the Courier, as
  that is proprietary information as well as outside the scope of the contract
  between the Courier and the City, which is for print only. She did, however,
  say that she was more than willing to provide these metrics.
  b. Karen & Michael Villalpando: Publishers of the Beverly Press
  i. Karen Stated that the rates that they were paid in the last fiscal year were
  unfair and that staff should reconsider them. She argued that the
  newspapers should be judged based on coverage and circulation for areas
  reached both in Beverly Hills and neighboring communities given how the
  things that the city is advertising can affect neighboring cities.
  ii. Michael then stated that rates should be determined by the number of
  households in the city, which he states is 14,388, versus circulation.
  Meanwhile they are currently being paid for 7,420 of the 13,800 papers that
  they circulate inside the city.
  iii. Some evidence they used to support their claim about the value of their
  circulation to surrounding communities is that at a recent city event,
  someone campaigning for the City Council elections found that 6 out of
  every 10 people they talked to were from outside the city.
  c. Josh Gross
  i. Agreed with everything Lisa said and would be ok with changing the audit
  dates.

  2) Discussion of Online Metrics Requirement for Future Audits, and review of the
  Annual Draft FY 2024-25 Advertising and Notices Bid:
  a. Presentation by Huma Ahmed.
 Highlights for February 26, 2024
Newspaper Ad Hoc Committee

  i. Per California contract code 20169 the city is required to annually release
  a formal bid for legal advertisements.
  ii. This bid is for locally adjudicated newspapers in the city of Beverly Hills
  iii. The three adjudicated newspapers are the Beverly Hills Weekly, the
  Beverly Hills Courier, and the Beverly Press.
  iv. On June 6, 2023, the City Council approved all three papers based on the
  following:
  1. The Courier won the willing bid while the other two would provide
  ads as needed.
  2. Rates were approved based on Beverly Hills circulation.
  3. Online metrics were approved but it was recommended that the
  Liaisons work out the details.
  v. The timelines for the FY 2024-25 are as follows:
  1. November: newspapers receive final audits from CVC.
  2. February: Ad Hoc Liaisons.
  3. March: release bid.
  4. April: finalize results.
  5. May: present to City Council at Study Session for approval.
  6. June: Consent item for City Council at formal session.
  vi. The budget for legal ads is $112,482 while display ads are budgeted at
  $537,058 for a total of $649,540.
  vii. CVC audits are good for two years, so an audit is not needed for this year.
  b. The Courier states that it usually takes around 3 weeks to complete their audit.\
  c. The Beverly Press conducts an ongoing audit and doesn’t see the reason for
  changing the audit date and does not support a change.
  d. The Weekly is fine with changing the audit date.
  e. The City Clerk stated that changing the date of the audit would not impact the city.
  f. If the audit was to be received in January, it would not give the city enough time to
  digest the information in time for the ad hoc committee meeting.
  g. The Courier runs a magazine every September and November, and conducting
  the audit during that time places additional strain on the Courier which is why the
  change was proposed.
  h. The online metrics were added in order to understand the demographic reach of
  the respective papers.
  i. Email media can consist of either e-notifications or alerts stating that the new
  edition of the paper is out.
  j. Councilmember Bosse is concerned about bots affecting the authenticity of social
  media statistics but trusts email and website analytics.
  k. The city has placed ads in other newspapers aside from the three above between
  1 and 5 times over the past year. Historically, non-adjudicated papers that the city
  has advertised with have consisted of the LA Times, the Jewish Journal, the LA
  Business Journal, and the Beverly Hills Living Magazine.
  l. The reasons for placing ads in non-adjudicated papers have been done because
  either the paper matched the targeted demographic the city was aiming for, or they
  reached out to the city and the city deemed it a good opportunity.
  m. Everyone in West Hollywood that was affected by changes in Beverly Hills water
  rates was individually noticed.
  n. The Courier sends around 5,000 newspapers to people outside of the City of
  Beverly Hills which go to surrounding communities.
  o. Roughly 2,800-3,300 Beverly Post papers are delivered to Beverly Hills residents
  through the LA times.
 Highlights for February 26, 2024
Newspaper Ad Hoc Committee

  p. The Post also now delivers 6,000 additional papers to the city on top of the 7,420
  from the last audit.
  q. The city used to break the display ads into two categories, one solely for Beverly
  Hills residents and ones for the surrounding community as well.
  r. The city switched off from this system as they found it unworkable.
  s. Display advertising can overlap with legal advertising, as in the case of public
  hearings.
  t. Display advertising is not required to be in a locally adjudicated newspaper, just
  legal ads.
  u. The current contract stipulates that legal ads must be placed in the Courier with
  the city being able to choose when to display them in the other two papers.

  3) Future Agenda Items:
  a. The Weekly wishes to revisit the total spend, as they want the total spend to reflect
  audited circulation.
  b. The Post wishes to discuss the rates they are being paid to include the display ads
  that are being distributed outside the city of Beverly Hills.

  4) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: February 26, 2024 / 5:52 PM
